title: A study to compare how well rocbrutinib works and how safe it is compared to Jaypirca® (pirtobrutinib) in participants with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma that has come back or did not respond to previous treatment of using covalent Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitors
official: A Phase 3 Open-Label, Randomized, Multicenter Study of Rocbrutinib (LP-168) vs Pirtobrutinib in Covalent BTK Inhibitor (cBTKi) Pretreated Relapsed or Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) / Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma (SLL) Subjects
summary: Main objective: To evaluate progression-free survival (PFS) of rocbrutinib compared to pirtobrutinib.
conditions: Relapsed or Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) / Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma (SLL)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Male or female subjects, ≥ 18 years of age at the time of screening
2. 10. Subjects must have adequate bone marrow independent of growth factor support per local laboratory reference range at screening as follows: •	Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) ≥1000/uL unless if neutropenia is due to heavy bone marrow involvement (approximately 60% or more), growth factor may be used to achieve the ANC eligibility criteria per discussion between the Investigator and the Medical Monitor. •	Platelet count ≥ 50,000/µL - OR - Platelet count ≥ 30,000/ µL if thrombocytopenia is clearly due to underlying disease. •	Hemoglobin ≥8.0g/dL, and not achieved by transfusion within 14 days prior to the first dose of the study drug.
3. 11.	Females of childbearing potential (i.e., non-postmenopausal for at least 2 years or not surgically sterile) and non-sterile males must practice at least 1 of the following methods of birth control with their partner(s) throughout the study, not donate oocyte, not father a child during treatment and for 90 days after the last dose of study treatment: •	Total abstinence from sexual intercourse as the preferred lifestyle of the subject; periodic abstinence is not acceptable. •	Surgically sterile partner(s) by vasectomy, bilateral orchiectomy, bilateral tubal ligation, bilateral oophorectomy or hysterectomy. •	Intrauterine device. •	Hormonal contraceptives (oral, parenteral, vaginal ring or transdermal) associated with inhibition of ovulation initiated for at least 1 month prior to study drug administration.
4. 12. Females of childbearing potential must have a negative pregnancy result as follows: •	At Screening on a serum sample obtained within 7 days prior to the first study drug administration. •	Prior to dosing on a urine or serum sample obtained on the first day of study drug administration if it has been > 7 days since obtaining the serum pregnancy test results in Screening. •	If a urine pregnancy test at any timepoint during the study is positive or indeterminate, a serum pregnancy test will be performed for confirmation.
5. 13. Male subjects must refrain from sperm donation, from initial study drug administration until 90 days after the last dose of study drug.
6. 14. The subject must be able to understand and voluntarily sign and date an informed consent, approved by an IRB (or ethics committee), prior to any protocol-related procedure.
7. 2. Histologically or cytologically confirmed R/R CLL/SLL that meets 2018 iwCLL criteria for systemic treatment.
8. 3. At least one measurable lesion including at least 1 of the following:  •	Enlarged lymph node with the longest diameter (LDi) ≥ 1.5 cm for CLL and > 1.5 cm for SLL. •	Enlarged extranodal lesion with LDi  > 1.0 cm for SLL.
9. 4. Previously have received a covalent BTK (cBTK) inhibitor, investigational or approved, and either alone or in combination with other agents. Subjects may have received an unlimited number of lines of prior therapy. The outcome of prior cBTKi and reason for stopping will be captured in detail.
10. 5.Known 17p deletion status (wildtype for 17p locus or positive for 17p deletion) by FISH •	If 17p deletion is positive, subject is no longer required to wait for TP53 mutation status during screening before randomization, but TP53 mutation status by NGS is still required. •	If 17p deletion is negative, subject is required to wait for TP53 mutation status during screening before randomization.
11. 6. 	Known TP53 mutation status by NGS. •	If TP53 mutation is positive, subject is no longer required to wait for 17p deletion status during screening before randomization, but 17p deletion status by FISH is still required. •	If TP53 mutation is negative, subject is required to wait for 17p deletion status during screening before randomization.
12. 7. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group ECOG performance status score ≤ 2.
13. 8. Predicted life expectancy ≥ 24 weeks.
14. 9. Subject must have adequate coagulation, renal and hepatic function per local laboratory reference ranges at Screening as follows: 	Activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and prothrombin time (PT) not to exceed 1.5 × ULN. 	Calculated creatinine clearance (CrCl) ≥30 mL/min using 24-hour CrCl OR Cockcroft-Gault formula: 	CrCl=  ((140-Age)×Actual Weight (kg)×[1=Male,0.85=Female])/(72×Serum Creatinine (mg/dL)) Or, if serum creatinine is in μmol/L: 	CrCl=  ((140-Age)×Actual Weight (kg)×[1.23=Male,1.04=Female])/(Serum Creatinine (µmol/L)) 	Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤ 3.0 ×ULN; bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × ULN (except subjects with Gilbert's Syndrome, who may have a bilirubin > 1.5 × ULN, per discussion between the Investigator and the Medical Monitor).
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Subjects who had prior non-covalent BTKi (ncBTKi) or BTK PROTAC.
2. 25. Subject has a significant history of renal, neurologic, psychiatric, pulmonary, endocrine, metabolic, immunologic, cardiovascular, or hepatic disease that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would adversely affect his/her participation in this study.
3. 26. Any conditions that affect the subject’s ability to swallow the drug, as well as conditions that seriously affect the absorption or pharmacokinetic parameters of the trial drug, including known malabsorption syndrome, disease significantly affecting gastrointestinal function, resection of the stomach or small bowel, ulcerative colitis, symptomatic inflammatory bowel disease, or partial or complete bowel obstruction.
4. 2. Histologically confirmed or suspected Richter's transformation.
5. 11. Subject requires treatment with systemic acid-reducing agents, H2 blocking agent and proton pump inhibitors, with the following exceptions: •	Proton pump inhibitors should be discontinued at least 14 days or at least 5-half-lives (whichever is shorter) prior and held throughout the study. •	If concurrent use of an H2 blocking agent is necessary, it must be administered only between 2 and 3 hours after the dose of rocbrutinib. If not taken during this time, the dose of H2 blocking agents should not be taken again until 2 – 3 hours after the next dose of rocbrutinib. •	If concurrent use of a local antacid is necessary, it must be administered 2 or more hours before and/or 2 or more hours after the dose of rocbrutinib.
6. 12. Requirement for immediate cytoreduction. However, subjects may receive up to two days of steroids for symptoms of impending organ impairment and remain eligible.
7. 14. Subjects who have undergone autologous/allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) therapy within 60 days of the first dose, or subjects on immunosuppressive therapy post-HSCT at the time of Screening, or currently with clinically significant graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) as per treating physician (Subjects in relapse after allogeneic transplantation must be off treatment with systemic immunosuppressive agents for at least 4 weeks. The use of topical steroids and/or up to 20 mg/day prednisone or equivalent systemic steroids for ongoing GVHD is permitted.).
8. 15. Subjects who have undergone major surgery or suffered severe trauma within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug.
9. 16. Subject has a history of other active malignancies within the past 1 year prior to study entry, with the exception of: •	Solid tumors on systemic treatment, such as breast cancer or prostate cancer on endocrine therapy, with stable disease (no progression, no escalation in systemic treatment for at least 2 years). •	Adequately treated in situ carcinoma of the cervix uteri. •	Basal cell carcinoma of the skin or localized squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. •	Previous malignancy confined and surgically resected (or treated with other modalities) with curative intent. •	Cancer with expected survival of 2 years or more or that will not confound evaluation of study treatment.
10. 17. Subjects who have any serious and/or uncontrolled systemic diseases and are judged by the investigator to be unsuitable to participate in this study (including active clinical serious infections ≥ CTCAE grade 2, hypertension that cannot be controlled by drugs), diabetes, unstable angina, congestive heart failure, respiratory diseases that require continuous oxygen inhalation, severe vascular embolism, uncontrollable massive bleeding or bleeding in important organs, severe liver, kidney or metabolic diseases, such as cirrhosis, kidney failure, etc.).
11. 18. Subjects with ongoing drug-induced liver injury.
12. 19. Subject has significant cardiovascular disease such as uncontrolled or symptomatic arrhythmias, congestive heart failure, or myocardial infarction or stroke within 180 days prior to the first dose of study drug, or any Class 3 or 4 cardiac disease as defined by the New York Heart Association Functional Classification or left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%.
13. 27. Other conditions that are not suitable for participating in this trial per Investigator’s judgement.
14. 28. A female subject who is pregnant
15. 30. Those who are allergic to rocbrutinib or pirtobrutinib and any of its components; those who are intolerant to rocbrutinib or pirtobrutinib.
16. 3.Confirmed prolymphocytic leukemia.
17. 4. Subjects who have received the following treatments within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is shorter) prior to the first dose of study drug, or has not recovered to ≤ Grade 1 clinically significant adverse effect(s)/toxicity(s) of the previous therapy (except for hematological toxicities, or other toxicities that, after discussion between the Investigator and the Sponsor, are considered to pose no safety risk to subjects): •	Any anti-cancer therapy including chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, biologic or immunotherapy, radiotherapy, myelosuppressive chemotherapy etc.  •	Any investigational therapy, including targeted small molecule agents. •	For CLL/SLL subjects who come off BCR antagonist (BTK inhibitors, PI3K inhibitors, etc.,) treatment, allow washout for 2 days as these subject’s progress quickly after treatment discontinuation and then remain eligible (steroids may be given during these two days to allow disease control).
18. 5. Subject has received following medications within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is shorter) prior to the first dose: •	Cytochrome P450, family 3, subfamily A (CYP3A4) strong inhibitors and strong CYP2C8 inducers/inhibitors. •	Potent CYP3A4 inducers such as rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, and St. John's wort.
19. 6.Subject has received the following medications, therapies, or natural products within 7 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is shorter) prior to the first dose: •	Steroid therapy (at dosages equivalent to prednisone >20 mg/day) for anti-neoplastic intent (except as noted in exclusion criterion #12).   •	Immunosuppressive drugs (equivalent to >10mg/day prednisone) for underlying autoimmune or rheumatologic conditions. •	There is a 3-months washout period required for subjects who have had prior CAR-T treatment if there is no evidence of cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or other adverse events related to the CAR-T treatment per discussion with the Medical Monitor; reduced washout period may be acceptable after discussion with Medical Monitor.
20. 7. Subject requires ongoing treatment of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers, or CYP2C8 sensitive substrates.
21. 8. Subject requires drugs that are known to cause QTc interval prolongation or torsade.
22. 9. Subject requires ongoing anti-coagulation with warfarin or other vitamin K antagonists.
23. 13. Subjects with clinically active involvement of the central nervous system (CNS). subjects with history of CNS involvement who have no symptoms suggestive of CNS disease and have had at least 2 successful lumbar punctures without cytologic evidence of leukemia may be included after discussion and approval of the Medical Monitor. (Evaluation of cerebrospinal fluid is only required if there is a clinical suspicion of CNS involvement by leukemia during screening in subjects without a history of CNS involvement).
24. 29.	A female subject who is breastfeeding, or who plans to breastfeed at any time from the first dose of study drug until 1 week after the last dose.
25. 10. Subject has consumed grapefruit, grapefruit products, Seville oranges (including marmalade containing Seville oranges), or Star fruit within 3 days prior to the first dose of study drug.
26. 20. Subject has significant screening electrocardiogram (ECG) abnormalities including 2nd degree AV block type II, 3rd degree block, Grade 2 or higher bradycardia. Subject has baseline prolongation of the heart rate-corrected QT (QTcF) interval ≥ 480 ms (calculated per Fridericia's formula [QTcF = QT/RR (1/3)]; in subjects with a QRS duration > 110 ms, calculated per QTcF adjusted formula for the widened QRS duration: Adjusted QTcF = measured QTcF - [measured QRS- 90 ms] ), a cardiovascular disability status of New York Heart Association Class ≥ 3 or associated other significant screening ECG or ultrasonic cardiogram abnormalities, per Investigator’s judgement. For any subject with underlying RBBB or LBBB, cardiology review is needed to correct QTcF calculation using Sponsor recommended formula below. Subjects with pacemaker will not be excluded as their QTc is artificially prolonged and can't be accurately measured with any formula.
27. 21. 	Subject exhibits evidence of other clinically significant uncontrolled condition(s) including, but not limited to: •	Uncontrolled systemic active bacterial, fungal, viral or parasitic infection.• Known poorly controlled human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) regardless of CD4 count, or active hepatitis B or C infection (active hepatitis B defined as detectable hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA in a subject who is HBsAg positive or HBcAb positive; active hepatitis C defined as HCV antibody positive with HCV RNA positive).   •	Exception: subjects who are HBsAg positive or HBcAb positive with undetectable HBV DNA are eligible provided they receive antiviral prophylaxis and HBV DNA monitoring per Section 8.5.4. •	Unexplained fever > 38.3°C within 7 days prior to the first dose of study drug administration (if the fever is considered attributed to the subject’s malignancy or an explained infection, the Subject may be enrolled at the discretion of the Investigator). •	Known active cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection."
28. 22. Subjects who receive live attenuated vaccines within 4 weeks before the first dose or plan to receive live attenuated vaccines during the study or within 4 weeks after the end of study treatment.
29. 23. Bleeding diseases (such as von Willebrand's disease, hemophilia A, hemophilia B, etc.) or history of intracranial hemorrhage within 180 days prior to the first dose of study drug.
30. 24. Autoimmune disease that is uncontrollable or requires more than 20 mg of prednisone (or other equivalent glucocorticoids) per day to be controlled within 4 weeks before the first medication.
